uncited: Brick Caching and Memory Management organizes volume data into fixed-size blocks (bricks) and manages their transfer between slow storage and fast rendering memory.
It solves limited capacity and high latency by maintaining a working set of frequently accessed bricks and evicting unused ones.

It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Bricking](914-bricking.md) (which defines the grid structure) and [Raymarching with LOD-based Brick Caching](5776-raymarching-with-lod-based-brick-caching.md) (which optimizes traversal) by focusing specifically on the dynamic allocation, eviction policies, and hierarchical storage tiers of the brick data itself.
A shared cache between brick map geometric primitives and brick map textures, as they use the same underlying data structure.
The brick cache size can be changed using the `Option "limits" "brickmemory"` command in the RIB file, or specified in the `rendermn.ini` file using the syntax `/prman/brickmemory`.
The `brickmemory` parameter specifies the cache size in kilobytes, with a default of 10 MB per thread (e.g., 10240 KB).
The RIB Option overrides the `rendermn.ini` setting if both are specified.
Cuts arbitrarily large volumes into $32^3$ bricks which are rendered separately.
The resulting brick images are composited together in image space in the correct order.
Optionally, volume traversal can be restricted to a cuboid subvolume to render a subset of a larger volume.

Hardware implementations historically supported 128 MB of volume storage (a $32^3$ volume of 8-bit voxels), with driver software handling automatic swapping of volume data to and from host memory for larger datasets.
